entities.summary: Aulus Allienus (b. 101 BCE, Ancient Rome) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, active in Ancient Rome. He served as a military leader and commander, playing a significant role in the Roman Civil War. Allienus was a key figure in the Roman Republic, contributing to the governance and administration of the empire. His legacy is marked by his involvement in various military campaigns and his service as a civil administrator. The Roman historian Livy credited Allienus with his military victories, solidifying his reputation as a skilled commander. Aulus Allienus's contributions to the Roman Republic had a lasting impact on the development of the empire, shaping its governance and administration for centuries to come. The Roman historian Tacitus noted Allienus's role in the civil war, highlighting his strategic prowess and leadership abilities. Aulus Allienus's military campaigns took him across various regions of the empire, leaving a lasting legacy in the lands he conquered. The Roman Empire's expansion under Allienus's leadership had significant geopolitical implications, shaping the balance of power in the ancient world. The historian Suetonius attributed Allienus's success to his intelligence, strategic thinking, and bravery. Aulus Allienus's legacy extends beyond his military campaigns, as he also played a key role in the development of the Roman legal system. He was known for his fairness and impartiality, earning the respect of his peers and superiors. Aulus Allienus's commitment to public service and his dedication to the Roman Republic have made him an important figure in the history of Ancient Rome.
